title: The use of fitness-fatigue models for sport performance modelling: conceptual issues and contributions from machine-learning
authors: Imbach F, Sutton-Charani N, Montmain J, Candau R, Perrey S
population: Not applicable (conceptual review on FFMs and machine learning)
findings: FFMs describe performance with first-order transfer functions representing antagonistic fitness and fatigue responses to training and allow determination of the optimal sequence of training doses.
Their efficiency for describing and predicting performance remains mitigated, attributed to simplified physiology and a univariate treatment of performance determinants.
Embedding physiological representations of training effects into non-linear, multivariate learning algorithms (ensemble methods) may surpass FFM weaknesses.
The authors conclude machine learning is not an alternative to FFMs but a way to take advantage of physiology-based models within powerful machine-learning models.
limitations: Perspective article without new data or quantitative comparison.
implications: Architecture: use FFM-derived features (fitness, fatigue, EWMA loads) as inputs to a multivariate regularised model that can also take sleep, HRV, temperature and age, rather than FFM alone.
Keep the physiology-based layer so outputs stay interpretable.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, Sports Med Open, 2022-03-03. Findings match Europe PMC abstract.
